attribution.note: Marcus wrote this sardonic 'Translation' of Murati's March 2024 statement in his own post and endorses it. It is his gloss, not a quote of Murati.

semantics.note: The phrasing is satirical, but it asserts something factual: Sora was trained on some licensed material plus other material whatever its licence status. The normalisation keeps that scope.

contract.note: Reading 'licensed or not' as including some unlicensed copyrighted material is the ordinary reading, and it isn't stretched. Separating unlicensed use from illegal use is fair. The result turns on missing evidence, not on interpretation.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous report (2024-03-14) that Murati confirmed Shutterstock licensed data was used. This supports only the licensed half.
A company disclosure about the December 2024 release describing mixed data sources. It gives no source-level licensing status and is not clearly about the March model.
A 2026 complaint alleging YouTube scraping, partly on information and belief. These are allegations, not findings, and it doesn't pin the conduct to the March 2024 model.

reviews.rationale: The licensed part is supported by the Shutterstock confirmation (e1). The unlicensed part, which is the core of the claim, is backed only by allegations in a 2026 complaint and a vague later company disclosure. Nothing in the packet reliably shows that unlicensed copyrighted material was used to train the March 2024 Sora. Nothing contradicts it either, so the claim is unresolved.
